title: migration.run task payload (v1)
description: Input for the migration agent's migration.run skill — PRD part-5. Fields are deliberately 1:1 with the Make.com runtime vars so the makecom backend is a pure pass-through.

sourceLocation.description: Source to migrate — incl. content-gen synthetic source URLs

folder.description: Explicit target folder (verbatim, no batch prefix/postfix) — generated drafts land here, e.g. 'ai-articles'. When set it overrides the migration-batch-* default. Keep generated content OUT of curated reference paths like /ai-content.

neighborPageUrl.description: A reference page (best-practice exemplar) the migrator GETs to learn this site's block conventions and editorial look — e.g. the canonical article it should mimic.

pattern.description: Prompt variant. 'article' authors a journal article (Theme: paper + Template: article; hero + stats + quote + author-bio) mimicking neighborPageUrl; 'generic' is the structural-fidelity default.

backend.description: Which runtime executes the migration. The Agent Card hides this — same skill, same artifact. 'dryrun' simulates (scaffold/testing).

model.description: Model to drive for this run, interpreted by the backend. opencode: a Kimi id ('kimi-for-coding' = K2.7 Coding, 'k3'), overriding KIMI_MODEL_ID — must be declared in opencode's provider.kimi-code.models map. sdk: a Claude model ('sonnet' | 'opus' | 'haiku' or a full model id), overriding CLAUDE_MIGRATION_MODEL. Other backends ignore it.

guidance.description: Operator guiding principles (free text) appended to the migration prompt — e.g. 'if an image is low-res, find a higher-res variant of the same image; record a gap if none exists'. Followed within the run's step budget; unsatisfiable principles are recorded in the report's gaps. Honored by the opencode and sdk backends; other backends ignore it.

memoryPath.description: The site's agent-memory page as a da.live source path (/source/{owner}/{site}/{page}.html). The opencode/sdk/dryrun backends READ it before the run (needs DALIVE_MCP_URL in the agent) and inject it into the prompt as lessons from previous runs; the model reports new 'lessons' in its final report, which the coordinator feeds to eval.reflect. Never fatal: a missing/unreadable page is recorded on the result's 'memory' field and the run continues.
